evidence.read: Original authors' 2017 manuscript pages 1-3: experimental configuration, autocorrelation-derived escape rates, low/high damping limits, theory comparison.
evidence.supports: Low damping limits energy transfer from the bath; high damping limits spatial diffusion. The optical nanoparticle experiment varies gas damping and resolves a maximum. Correlated recrossings and changes of potential are explicitly controlled.

evidence.read: Original 1997 PRL pages 1-3, equation 2, definition of the repeated switching experiment, weak-coupling condition and rare-event sampling caveat.
evidence.supports: Negative-temperature-normalized work exponential average gives the free-energy difference via its logarithm, provided each realization starts from the same canonical equilibrium. Rare low-work trajectories can dominate and cause severe finite-sample errors.

additional_evidence_read.title: Equilibrium information from nonequilibrium measurements in an experimental test of Jarzynski's equality
additional_evidence_read.supports: Original 2002 RNA pulling experiment demonstrates recovery from irreversible work; abstract only, not a reanalysis of trajectories.

evidence.read: Original authors' 2014 paper, Background on page 2: MHC integral, uniform density-of-states assumption, comparison with Marcus and Butler-Volmer rates, explanation of disappearance of the inverted region.
evidence.supports: Occupied metal states below the Fermi level continue to supply low-barrier electron transfer at large overpotential, giving a reaction-limited current rather than Marcus inversion. The card distinguishes this from mass-transfer limitation.

additional_evidence_read.title: Free energy and temperature dependence of electron transfer at the metal-electrolyte interface
additional_evidence_read.supports: Chidsey's original 1991 self-assembled monolayer electrode experiment and fitted reorganization energy; abstract only.

evidence.read: Publisher-indexed abstract and introduction of original Ren, Qu and Li 2001 paper.
evidence.supports: Pressure transport of double-layer ions builds a streaming field, which drives counterflow and changes measured flow resistance. Paired streaming-potential and pressure/flow measurements are reported. This does not identify every anomalous microchannel pressure loss as electroviscous.
